acilis-bilgi: These are the opening words of the Nutuk, the speech Mustafa Kemal Atatürk delivered over 36 and a half hours at the Second Congress of the Republican People's Party on 15–20 October 1927. It tells the story of the National Struggle and the founding of the Republic through its documents. This map follows that journey, from his departure from İstanbul on 16 May 1919 to the proclamation of the Republic on 29 October 1923. Source: Nutuk–Söylev, I. Cilt, s. 2, T.C. Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığı e-kitap (ekitap.ktb.gov.tr); A. İlgazi, Atatürk Araştırma Merkezi Dergisi. Quotations from the Nutuk are translated for this site; the original Turkish is shown with each.

hk-nasil-liste:
• The map shows the turning points of the period and the journeys connecting them. Intermediate stops are not shown as points; the route passes through them.
  • Drag or play the timeline at the bottom and the map moves to that day. Days on the road and days with no events are skipped during playback.
  • The orange ring shows where he was that day. During a journey it stays at the place of departure and moves to the next point on arrival.
  • The colour of a route shows how he travelled; where the sources do not say, the line is grey. The emphasised line is the latest journey. The colours come from the colour-blind friendly Okabe-Ito palette.
  • "Start the journey" switches to the 3D view: the camera follows the route, a vehicle moves along it, and at each stop subtitles tell what happened there. Where the means of travel is unknown, the vehicle is semi-transparent.
hk-yollar-metin: The roads of those years no longer exist; the lines follow today's road and railway equivalents of the same route. Sea routes are approximate. The steamer, car and train in the 3D view are models evoking the vehicles of the period; a vehicle's position on the route is estimated from the start and end dates of the journey.
lejant-not: Lines follow today's equivalent of the route. The emphasised line is the latest journey; faded lines are earlier routes.
pp-cizgi: The line follows today's equivalent of the route.
